newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to start satellite crop forecast mid-1997.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to start satellite crop forecast mid-1997.

text.p: Hungary will start experimental satellite crop prediction in mid-1997, a researcher said on Monday.

The Land Measurement and Telemetry Institute (FTI) plans to base its service on images from two American satellites, (NOAA and Landsat) and one French (Spot) satellite, FTI's Gabor Csornai told Reuters.

"It will be the result of research started almost 20 years ago," he said, adding that in the first, experimental phase the sole client and sponsor will be the Ministry of Agriculture but they plan to develop the project into a commercially viable service.
In the second phase FTI expects to have main grain producers, traders and distributors as clients.
"The system would be capable of predicting crops on areas as small as 1,000 hectares, but it would not be worth acquiring images for such a small batch," Csornai said.
He added that once the system is up and running, food producers or even individual farmers could use their services as the project is sector-neutral. --Denes Albert, Budapest newsroom +36 1 327 4040
